content:
The threshold for pair production occurs when the invariant mass squared of the two-photon system equals the square of the total rest mass of the electron-positron pair. For a head-on collision, the invariant mass squared is \(s = 4E\varepsilon\), where \(E\) is the high-energy photon energy and \(\varepsilon\) is the CMB photon energy. The threshold condition is \(s = (2m_e c^2)^2 = 4m_e^2 c^4\), giving \(E = m_e^2 c^4 / \varepsilon\).

Using \(m_e c^2 = 511\ \text{keV} = 5.11 \times 10^5\ \text{eV}\) and \(\varepsilon = 10^{-3}\ \text{eV}\):
\[
E = \frac{(5.11 \times 10^5\ \text{eV})^2}{10^{-3}\ \text{eV}} = \frac{2.61 \times 10^{11}\ \text{eV}^2}{10^{-3}\ \text{eV}} = 2.61 \times 10^{14}\ \text{eV} = 2.6 \times 10^5\ \text{GeV}.
\]

This matches option (B). The note warns against mistakenly doubling the result, which would occur if one incorrectly used \(E = 2m_e^2/\varepsilon\) or a different CMB energy.

Answer: B
